hero.name: Jinhong Yu
hero.thesis: I build teleoperation, mixed-reality and data-capture systems that turn human demonstrations into robot training data.
hero.intro: As founding robotics engineer at Theta‑intelligence, I built a Meta Quest teleoperation platform and its real-time streaming layer. I also built handheld and egocentric data-collection systems. With a mechanical engineering degree and an M.S. in AI, my work ranges from CAD and wiring to Unity, perception and model fine-tuning.

experienceSection.title: Experience
experienceSection.intro: Robotics, XR and AI engineering, most recently full-stack web development.

points.text: Building an e-commerce platform: a store-management back office for merchants and a customer-facing WeChat Mini Program.

points.label: Teleoperation
points.text: Built the Meta Quest teleoperation app (Unity, OpenXR), with mixed-reality UI and external UVC camera support. Its real-time layer streams video, audio and control between robots, headsets and operator stations, with commands at 200 Hz and video at 30 fps.

points.label: Data collection
points.text: Designed and integrated two capture rigs: Quest-tracked handheld UMI grippers and an egocentric rig. Synchronized pipelines on Raspberry Pi and Quest record video, sensor and IoT data.

points.label: Edge AI
points.text: Wrote Android native plugins that run ONNX models on Quest, including sherpa-onnx text-to-speech. Deployed voice-driven AI agents on ESP32 (ESP-Claw) and Raspberry Pi (zero-Claw).
Fine-tuned Stable Diffusion on limited GPU hardware using LoRA and model parallelism.
Deployed a text-to-video pipeline aimed at multi-character scenes with consistent characters, and supported the team's text-to-image and text-to-video experiments.
Graded coursework, held office hours and gave a guest lecture on diffusion models.
Set up lab servers for research projects, and designed, implemented and ran experiments for the project leads.
